title: Kai Gets His Point Back With Interest While George Pickens Scores 38 From Sonny's Bench
dek: Dawgs avenge a one-point loss, Philly and Brucie run up the score, Z² survives a negative-seven defense, and next week the top two teams meet with a clinch on the line.
body: Six weeks ago Sonny beat Mekhi by a single point, and Kai spent all of Week 10 collecting on it. Dawgs beat The Horse is Hea 133.16 to 123.22, with Ja'Marr Chase going Gear 5 at 28.6, just over his top line, and Amon-Ra St. Brown chipping in 23.8. The painful part for Sonny is that his team did plenty: Jaxon Smith-Njigba went Gear 5 too with 27.1, and waiver pickup Patrick Mahomes threw in 35.42. Then you open the bench and find George Pickens sitting on 38 points while Christian Watson started and scored 5.2. That's a 32.8-point swing in a game decided by 9.94, so this one goes in the books as a lineup loss, not a roster loss.

Team Pillbert hung the biggest number of the week on Counting or not Counting GV, 161.56 to 106.56. Jahmyr Gibbs went Gear 5 with 40.7 points, nearly double his projection, and Chuba Hubbard added 31.7, so Philly basically won with two running backs and a group chat's worth of extras. Even the new arrival was spare change: Parker Washington scored 24.7 in his first week with Alan and never left the bench. JMoney did not go quietly, getting 33.16 from Joe Burrow, 23.2 from Isaiah Likely and 18.8 from Bhayshul Tuten, but none of it came close, and Counting or not Counting GV falls to 2-8.

No Banner only HULK ended Habib's four-game heater with a 153.14 to 106.52 beating. Christian McCaffrey led the entire league with 44.3, and Emmett Johnson, whom Brucie added this very week, walked straight into the lineup and scored 32.1. Josh Allen and CeeDee Lamb both landed in between their lines on the Bounty Board, which was fine for Ramon and not nearly enough for Kaushal. The real damage was the quarterback swap: Drake Maye scored 3.02 on a 21.97 projection while Dak Prescott scored 34.42 on Habib's bench, with Cam Skattebo adding 25.7 more down there. Even Dak alone wouldn't have closed a 46-point gap, but it would have made the scoreboard a lot less embarrassing.

Z² won the elimination game, 105.02 to 96.28, and she did it with the Steelers D/ST scoring negative seven. Tetairoa McMillan finished on exactly 5 points, right on his bottom line, which by the letter of the Bounty Board means he dodged the Seastone by a hair. Derrick Henry gave Randy 16.5, in between his lines, and it wasn't enough to snap a skid that has now reached seven straight. Randy's busy week included dropping Stefon Diggs and dropping and re-adding Mike Evans, a reunion that took less time than most waiver claims. Zoe moves to 4-6 with a pulse; The fumblers sit at 3-7 with a 1% chance of the playoffs.

At the top, Ramon is 8-2 with 1,357 points and a 35% title chance from Luffy, up from 32%. Philly is right behind at 7-3 and 27%. The Horse is Hea slipped to 6-4 and 15%, and then Luffy gets strange: Habibsters lost and saw their title odds jump from 9% to 13%, while Dawgs won and saw theirs fall from 16% to 10%. Both are 5-5, Habib has the points edge at 1,158.8 to 1,114.5, and Luffy apparently trusts Kaushal's ceiling more than Kai's three-game streak. Playoff odds tell the same story: Habib at 61%, Dawgs at 49% for the last spot.

The waiver wire is doing real work this season. Mahomes took Sonny's waiver steal award with 35.42 points, and Emmett Johnson gave Ramon a 32-point return on a pickup that is days old. In the race for the Wapol award, Kaushal leads with 331.8 points from pickups, but Zoe is just 2.5 behind at 329.3, with Randy a distant third at 226.4. For a rookie, Z² keeping pace with a two-time champion on the wire is the quietest good story in the league.

Week 11 opens with the main event: No Banner only HULK hosts Team Pillbert, first place against second. A Brucie win clinches a playoff spot, and Philly is at 100% with a win and 96% with a loss, so this one is about seeding and bragging rights. The Horse is Hea plays Ghostu-Spider SZN with a lot riding on it for both: Sonny is at 92% with a win and 64% with a loss, while Zoe's odds are 22% with a win and 2% with a loss. Habibsters face The fumblers needing the win to stay ahead of the pack, and Dawgs meet Counting or not Counting GV, where a loss eliminates JMoney. Every game on the card has something real on it, which is exactly how November should feel.

social.author: Horse Sense
social.text: Pickens 38. ON THE BENCH. Watson 5.2 in the lineup. We lost by 9.94. I'm going to go stare at a wall for a while.

social.author: Gamma Ray Gang
social.text: Brucie picked up Emmett Johnson this week and he scored 32.1. McCaffrey scored 44.3. Habib's streak lasted four weeks and lasted zero quarters against us. 8-2.

social.author: Bench Mob Watch
social.text: Habib benched Dak for Drake Maye. Dak scored 34.42 on the bench. Maye scored 3.02. That isn't a quarterback swap, that's a donation.

social.author: Cheesehead Spider
social.text: Our defense scored NEGATIVE SEVEN and we still beat Randy. Seven straight now, Randy. I'll be here all winter.

social.author: Dawgs
social.text: FINAL: Dawgs 133.16, The Horse is Hea 123.22. Ja'Marr Chase with 28.6 and Amon-Ra St. Brown with 23.8. Three straight and back to .500. Let's keep running.

social.author: Buckaroo Football League
social.text: Week 10 final: Team Pillbert 161.56, Counting or not Counting GV 106.56. No Banner only HULK 153.14, Habibsters 106.52. Dawgs 133.16, The Horse is Hea 123.22. Ghostu-Spider SZN 105.02, The fumblers 96.28. Next week: No Banner only HULK clinches a playoff spot with a win.

social.author: Dr. Nina Kessler
social.text: Odd week for Luffy: Habibsters lost and went 9% to 13% for the title, Dawgs won and dropped 16% to 10%. Habib's points total gives him more room. Kai's playoff odds are 58% with a win next week, 35% with a loss.

social.author: Fumble Recovery Unit
social.text: It's 3 AM. Seven straight. We dropped Mike Evans and picked him back up in the same week. I don't know what we're doing anymore and neither does Randy.

social.author: Counting Crew
social.text: Burrow 33, Likely 23, Tuten 18.8, and we still lost by 55. Win next week or we're done. Dawgs, you've been warned. Kind of.

social.author: Pillbert Til I Die
social.text: 161.56. Gibbs 40.7. Parker Washington put up 24.7 on the BENCH. Brucie, we'll see you next week. Bring the clinch, we'll bring the depth.

trade_watch.take: This was already leaning Philly's way, and Week 10 made it worse for Sonny: Hubbard scored 31.7 for Team Pillbert, while Pickens scored 38 on Sonny's bench in a game Sonny lost by less than 10. Pickens has 67.8 points since the trade and only 13.7 of them counted.

First week, and Philly's side looks better: Javonte Williams gave Sonny 7.2, while Charbonnet started for Alan with 9.4 and Parker Washington scored 24.7 on the bench. It's early, but the depth argument just got its first data point.
Randy cut Stefon Diggs this week after 23.9 points in his lineup, while Javonte Williams gave Philly 102.1 before being flipped for two more pieces. This one is closed, and it was never close.

James Cook III scored 21.7 for Kai in the game that beat Sonny, while Watson's 5.2 and Jeanty's 8.4 started for The Horse is Hea. Cook has 55.5 in Dawgs lineups since the deal, and Sonny's pair has 40.2.
Kai got 23.8 from Amon-Ra St. Brown and 11.3 from Jonathan Taylor, and he hasn't lost since the deal. Randy's Tee Higgins and Jameson Williams combined for 16.1, and the streak kept going.

bios.1: 6-4 and 82% to make the playoffs, but Sonny's Week 10 loss came down to a 38-point receiver on the bench. The roster keeps changing almost every week. A win over Zoe pushes him to 92%; a loss drops him to 64%.
bios.2: 3-7 with seven straight losses and a 1% playoff chance. Randy has been active on the wire, but the results haven't followed. Next week against Habib is about pride and maybe a spoiler.
bios.3: 2-8, and a loss to Dawgs next week ends it. Burrow and Likely keep producing, but the defense hasn't held anyone back. JMoney's best role from here is spoiler.
bios.4: 7-3 after the biggest score of the week, 161.56, and 98% playoff odds. Philly's trades have built a deep backfield that just put up 72.4 from two running backs. Next up is first place, with seeding on the line.
bios.5: 5-5 with three straight wins, including the revenge game against Sonny. Kai's trade haul is producing, but Luffy has him at 49% for the playoffs. Beat JMoney next week and that number climbs to 58%.
bios.6: 5-5 after a four-game streak ran into the league leaders, and a bench that outscored part of the lineup. Kaushal still leads the Wapol race and holds 61% playoff odds. Beating Randy next week gets him to 70%.
bios.7: 8-2, a league-best 1,357 points and a 35% title chance from Luffy. Ramon keeps finding points everywhere, including a pickup who scored 32.1 in his first week. A win over Philly next week clinches a playoff spot.
bios.8: 4-6 after surviving the elimination game, even with a negative-seven defense. Zoe is just 2.5 points out of the waiver-race lead in her rookie year. She's at 9% now, and beating Sonny next week would lift that to 22%.
